findings.label: Focus and aria-pressed announcement lost on every chip repaint
findings.detail: refreshStrips() rebuilds container.innerHTML for every [data-reactions-for] strip in the thread, not just the changed one. It runs on the optimistic toggle, on the server response, and on reaction-only polls. The focused chip is detached, so keyboard focus drops to <body> and the next Tab restarts from the top of the page; a screen reader also never hears the state change, because the button carrying the new aria-pressed value is a different element than the one that was activated. Fix: capture the active chip's message id + emoji before the repaint and re-focus the equivalent chip (falling back to the .chat-reaction-add button when the chip disappears) - closeSheet() already does exactly this lookup for the add button - or mutate the existing chips' textContent/aria-* in place instead of replacing them.

findings.label: Pressed state signalled by colour alone
findings.detail: .chat-reaction-chip[aria-pressed="true"] differs from the default only in background, border-color and color. aria-pressed covers assistive tech, but a non-colour cue (border width, ring, or a leading check glyph) would satisfy WCAG 1.4.1 for sighted users with colour-vision deficiency.

findings.label: Unpressed chip border contrast ~1.25:1
findings.detail: rgba(0,0,0,0.10) on #ffffff. Disclosed by the implementer and consistent with .chat-bubble.from-them and .thread-row, so it introduces no new convention, but it will not pass a strict WCAG 1.4.11 non-text-contrast audit.

findings.label: No server-side throttle on the toggle endpoint
findings.detail: Debouncing is client-side only (the inFlight Set). UNIQUE (message_id, user_id, emoji) caps storage at six rows per user per message so there is no unbounded growth, and no rate-limiting infrastructure exists anywhere in server.js, but a participant can still spin the endpoint.

findings.label: Chat density: a 44px add button under every message
findings.detail: strip() always appends the add button, so every message grows by ~44px inside the max-height: 58vh message scroller and fewer messages fit on a phone screen. Consider revealing the add button on hover/focus on desktop, or collapsing the strip height when a message has no reactions.

findings.label: DDL and aggregation never executed against MySQL
findings.detail: No database was available, so the CREATE TABLE, the real GROUP BY and the DELETE/INSERT IGNORE are proven only as SQL text with bound parameters (the utf8mb4_bin collation trap is handled up front). Worth one npm run init-db plus a two-account smoke test before release.

checklist.1_privacy: PASS - both read paths go through buildReactionList(), which emits only {emoji,count,mine}; user_id/sender_id/username never appear in any response.
checklist.2_no_notifications: PASS - the new handler and the thread-GET addition reference no notifications table, no web-push, no activity feed, no is_read, and do not call notification-text.js.
checklist.3_auth_and_participation: PASS - requireAuth on the new endpoint; participation re-derived via anon_messages JOIN anon_threads with 403 'To nie Twoja rozmowa'; the thread aggregate is scoped by thread_id after the existing 403 check.
checklist.4_sql: PASS - every statement is pool.execute with ? placeholders; message id passes a ^[0-9]+$ regex before parseInt and reaches SQL as a number.
checklist.5_emoji_allowlist: PASS - isAllowedReactionEmoji() checked server-side before any query; off-list values get 400 'Nieprawidłowa reakcja'.
checklist.6_toggle: PASS - UNIQUE KEY uniq_message_user_emoji (message_id, user_id, emoji) in both DDLs; DELETE-then-INSERT IGNORE is idempotent and the response is the recomputed aggregate.
checklist.7_performance: PASS - one grouped query per thread load (no N+1); INDEX idx_reaction_message (message_id) present in both DDLs.
checklist.8_a11y: FAIL (blocking finding 1) - all other requirements met: real buttons, keyboard reachable, aria-pressed, gender-neutral Polish aria-labels, dialog role + aria-modal, Tab trap, Escape close, focus return from the sheet, prefers-reduced-motion at both breakpoints, HTML escaping via esc(). Chip repaints lose focus and never announce the state change.
checklist.9_polish_wording: PASS - gender-neutral sentence-case strings throughout; plurals via plCount(n,'osoba','osoby','osób'); no dodal(a) or masculine-only forms.
checklist.10_forbidden_files: PASS for this task - formularz.html, formularz.js, notification-text.js, sw.js and app-theme.css show as modified in git diff --stat, but grepping their diffs for reaction|reakcj|chat-reactions returns no matches; those edits are concurrent agents' work. Reaction CSS is entirely in the new public/chat-reactions.css, and the reaction-specific server.js footprint is four targeted additions, not a rewrite.
checklist.11_init_db: PASS - anon_threads, anon_messages and anon_message_reactions added to init-db.js (46 added lines, 0 removed) with definitions mirroring ensureAnonMessageTables() and cross-reference comments in both files.
